div.head: VI As 6.3
div.ab: ⁊ we cwædon be urum þeowum mannum [þam] þa men hæfdon: gif hine man forstæle, þæt hine man forgulde mid healfan punde; gif we ðonne gyld arærdon, þæt him man yhte ufon on þæt be his wlites weorðe; ⁊ hæfdon us þone oferéacan þe we þær abædon. Gif he hine þonne forstalede, þæt hine man lædde to þære torfunge, swa hit ǽr gecwedan wæs; ⁊ scute ælc man þ[e] man hæfde swa pænig swa healfne be þæs geferscípes mænio, swa man þæt weorð úparæran mihte. Gif he þonne oðseoce, þæt hine man forgulde be his wlites weorðe; ⁊ we ealle hine áxodan. Gif we him þonne tócuman moston, þæt him man dyde þæt ylce þe man þam Wyliscean þeofe dyde, oððe hine man anhó.

Diximus de seruis nostris, eis qui men habent: si furetur, soluatur X sol.; si autem gild erigamus, ut apprecietur super hoc secundum pretium suum, et habeamus nobis superplus, quod abhinc impetrabimus. Si denique furtum faciat, ducatur ad lapidandum, sicut ante dictum est; et mittat omnis qui men habeat (hominem habebit) sic denarium sic obolum secundum societatis admonicionem, sic ut hoc ualens colligi possit. Si neget (aufugiat), persoluatur pretio uultus sui, et omnes inquiramus illud (inde). Si assequi possimus, fiat ei quod de Walisco fure factum (sicut de seruo fure dictum) est, uel suspendatur.

⁊ we cwædon be urum þeowum mannum þa menn þa men hæfdon; gif hine man forstæle, þæt hine man forgulde mid healfan punde; gif we ðonne gyld arærdon, þæt him man yhte ufon on þæt be his wlites weorðe; and hæfdon us þone oferéacan þe we þær abædon. Gif he hine þonne forstalede, þæt hine man lædde to þære torfunge, swa hit ǽr gecwedan wæs; ⁊ scute ælc man þ[e] man hæfde swa pænig swa healfne be þæs gefersápes mænio, swa man þæt weorð úparæran mihte. Gif he þonne oðsceoce, þæt hine man forgulde be his wlites weorðe; ⁊ we ealle hine áxodan. Gif we him þonne tócuman moston, þæt him man dyde þæt ylce þe man þam Wyliscean þeofe dyde, oððe hine man anhó.

Und über unsere unfreien Leute haben wir denen, welche unfreie Leute halten, bestimmt: wenn jemand einen [unfreien] Menschen stiehlt, dass man ihn [aus unserer Kasse] mit einem halben Pfunde [dem Herrn] ersetze; wenn wir aber [den Dieb nachweisen und gerichtlichen] Ersatz erheben, dass man ihm [dem Herrn] über das [¹/₂ Pfund] hinaus, je nach Werthe der Beschaffenheit jenes [Sklaven, Geld zum Ersatz] hinzulege; und dass wir für uns den Überschuss behalten, den wir hierbei [gerichtlich] erlangen. Wenn aber der [Unfreie] sich selbst wegstahl, dass man ihn zur Steinigung führe, wie es vorher bestimmt worden ist; und jedermann, der (einen H) Sklaven hält, schiesse entweder einen Pfennig oder einen halben ein, je nach der Mitgliederzahl der Genossenschaft, so dass man jenen Werth [für den Herrn] aufbringen könne. Wenn er aber entkommt, dass man ihn [dem Herrn] ersetze nach Werth seiner Beschaffenheit; und dass wir alle die Nachforschung übernehmen. Wenn wir ihn dann bekommen können, thue man ihm dasselbe, was man dem nicht Englischfreien Diebe thut, oder man hänge ihn auf.

And concerning our unfree men, we have determined for those who keep unfree men: if anyone steals an [unfree] person, that he be paid for [to the lord, from our fund] with half a pound; but if we [trace the thief and] raise [legal] compensation, that he [the lord] be paid more on top of [the half pound], according to the value of the condition of that [slave]; and that we keep for ourselves the surplus which we obtain [in court] from it. But if the [unfree man] stole himself away, that he be led to stoning, as was determined before; and every man who keeps (a, H) slave is to contribute either a penny or a halfpenny, according to the number of members of the fellowship, so that that value can be raised [for the lord]. But if he escapes, that he be paid for [to the lord] according to the value of his condition; and that we all take up the search. If we can then get him, let the same be done to him as is done to the Welsh [i.e. non-English-free] thief, or let him be hanged.

With reference to our slaves, those of us who possess slaves have declared: if anyone steals a slave, half a pound shall be paid for him. If we succeed in getting payment, he [the owner] shall receive an additional sum according to the appearance of the slave, and we shall keep the surplus of what we are awarded in the suit. If, however, a slave runs away, he shall be taken out and stoned as has already been decreed. And each man who has a slave shall pay either a penny or a half-penny according to the numbers of the association, so as to make up the proper amount. If, however, he gets clean away, his lord shall be paid for him according to his appearance, and we shall all search for him. Then, if we can catch him, he shall receive the same treatment as a Welsh thief, or he shall be hanged.

And concerning our slaves, we pronounced to those who owned slaves that, if anyone were to steal a slave, half a pound was to be paid for him; if, however, we obtained compensation, he [the owner] was to be paid above that according to his value, judging by his appearance; and we were to have for ourselves the surplus of what we obtained there. If, however, he ran away, he was to be taken and stoned as it was formerly agreed; and each man who possessed a man was to contribute a penny or a halfpenny, according to the number of people in the association, so that the full sum should be reached. If, however, he should get away, he was to be paid for according to his value, judging by his appearance, and we were all to search for him. If we then should come across him, the same was to be done to him as was done to an unfree thief, or he is to be hanged.

div.note: ‘þa menn’ in H (‘men’ = slaves) was struck by Thorpe and Schmid as a dittography, but the archetype had ‘þam’ (Quadr.), which the scribe misread. ‘þ[e]’ is corrected from Quadr.; ‘men’ perhaps to be read from Quadr. H's ‘oðseoce’ is corrected by Toller (perhaps ‘oðsceote’). Liebermann compares IV As 6.5.

Nur wer ein Wertstück der Art des Verlorenen auch hat, steuert zur Versicherungskasse bei; die anderen laufen nicht die Gefahr solchen Verlustes. Vgl. Genossenschaft 12e
Only a man who also owns a valuable of the same kind as the one lost contributes to the insurance fund; the others do not run the risk of such a loss. Cf. Genossenschaft 12e
Vgl. Gl unfrei 7d; Menschenraub 1a. — Zu Q’s Schilling o. 6, 1⁴. — Der kleine Ersatz unter dem Wert tritt nur ein, wenn sich der Dieb nicht fand, die Gilde also keinen Prozessertrag gewann

Cf. Gl unfrei 7d; Menschenraub 1a. — On Q’s shilling, above 6, 1⁴. — The small compensation below the value applies only if the thief was not found, and the gild therefore gained no proceeds from a lawsuit

Diese Bed. fehlt Wbb. (Toller Suppl.) und ist verschieden von dem Sinne 17 Zeilen weiter ‘aufbringen’ (Mätzner: Mittelengl. von Summe, Heer). Schmid (und Price-Thorpe?) versteht als Empfänger Bestohlenen, als zahlend die Gilde. Vielmehr der Dieb zahlt, die klagende Gilde empfängt

This meaning is missing from the dictionaries (Toller Suppl.) and is different from the sense 17 lines further on, ‘raise’ (Mätzner: Middle English, of a sum, an army). Schmid (and Price-Thorpe?) takes the man robbed as recipient and the gild as payer. Rather, the thief pays and the prosecuting gild receives

Q lässt gyld als unverstanden stehen und him unübersetzt. — Die Gilde behält nicht alles über ½ £ Eingenommene (gegen Jastrow Sklaven 76), sondern erhöht dem Sklavenhalter den Ersatz bis zum Sklavenwerte hinauf und gewinnt nur den noch höheren Bussbetrag

Q leaves gyld standing as not understood and him untranslated. — The gild does not keep everything taken in above ½ £ (against Jastrow Sklaven 76), but raises the slave-owner’s compensation up to the value of the slave and gains only the still higher amount of the compensation
Richtig Q; ‘einforderten [von den Genossen]’ Schmid (und Price-Thorpe ‘require’); s. dagegen 6, 1⁹
Q is right; ‘demanded [from the members]’ Schmid (and Price-Thorpe ‘require’); see, against this, 6, 1⁹
Q missversteht wie Ine 24². — Dieser Stil hebt deutlich den Ggsatz hervor: gif hine man forstæle zu gif he hine þonne [‘dagegen’] forstalede
Q misunderstands, as at Ine 24². — This style clearly brings out the contrast: gif hine man forstæle as against gif he hine þonne [‘on the other hand’] forstalede

IV 6, 5 sprach vom Stehlen des Unfreien; davon ist Diebstahl begangen an sich selbst durch Entlaufen nur eine Unterart; Maurer Kr. Übsch. 410. Hier gibt die Gilde wieder dem Landrechte partikulare Ausführungsbestimmung

IV 6, 5 spoke of stealing an unfree man; of this, theft committed against oneself by running away is only a subspecies; Maurer Kr. Übsch. 410. Here the gild again gives the law of the land a particular implementing provision
‘mehrere Sklaven’ Q i, vielleicht besser
‘several slaves’ Q i, perhaps better
nicht ‘so — wie’; s. Wb 205 H; Toller 941 VI 2a. 940b V 2
not ‘so — as’; see Wb 205 H; Toller 941 VI 2a. 940b V 2
Q irrt, an manung oder mynegung denkend
Q errs, thinking of manung or mynegung

Genauer ‘der Sklavenhalter’, da nur diese (o. Erkl. 2) beisteuerten. Je nachdem ½ oder 1 Pf. gesammelt und ein Sklav von ½ £ oder 1 £ ersetzt ward, mussten 120—480 Sklavenhalter beisteuern, um die Gilde nicht verlieren zu lassen. Gab es mehr, so gewann sie den Überschuss. Die Leistung des Einzelnen sinkt mit der Zahl der Pflichtigen, wie o. 4⁸

More precisely ‘the slave-owners’, since only they (above note 2) contributed. According to whether ½ or 1 penny was collected and a slave of ½ £ or 1 £ was compensated, 120—480 slave-owners had to contribute if the gild was not to lose. If there were more, it gained the surplus. The individual’s contribution falls with the number of those liable, as above 4⁸
Den ganzen Sklavenpreis, nicht bloss jene Taxe von ½ £
The whole price of the slave, not merely that tariff of ½ £
Q hatte wie H einen Fehler des Archetyps vor sich und sah anfangs darin oðsace ‘leugnet’, errät aber dann aus dem Zusammenhang richtigen Sinn. Vgl. Wb: oðsceacan, utsceote
Q, like H, had before it an error of the archetype and at first saw in it oðsace ‘denies’, but then guesses the correct sense from the context. Cf. Wb: oðsceacan, utsceote
bessere Übs.: ‘ihn aufspüren, erkunden, nach ihm forschen’
better translation: ‘track him down, find him out, search for him’
‘unfreien’ Metcalfe English and Scandin. 90. Der Freie und Unfreie, aber nicht Engländer und Walliser (Gl 1; o. S. 74 Z. 2) ward in der Art der Todesstrafe (s. d. Gl 19) unterschieden

‘unfree’ Metcalfe English and Scandin. 90. The freeman and the unfree, but not the Englishman and the Welshman (Gl 1; above p. 74 l. 2), were distinguished in the manner of the death penalty (see that word in Gl 19)
Man steinige (s. d. Gl 1) ihn
Let him be stoned (see that word in Gl 1)
So Ine 24 gegen den entlaufenen Strafknecht
So Ine 24 against the runaway penal slave

I take the first þa men of the Anglo-Saxon text to be nominative in apposition to we; the second þa as nominative of the relative and the second men as accusative, meaning ‘slaves.’ Thorpe and Schmid regard the repetition of þa men as a scribal error, Liebermann emends the first þa men to þam. Quadr. reads Diximus de seruis nostris, eis qui men habent.
With Liebermann I take ‘our slaves’ as referring not to slaves of the association, but to the slaves owned by individual members.
See IV As. cap. 6 § 5.
i.e. the full value of a slave which was usually a pound (240 pence); cf. Ine, cap. 23 § 3, 74, 3 § 2; IV As. cap. 6 § 6.
This means he would be stoned to death (cf. IV As. cap. 6 § 5).
Cf. Ine, cap. 24.
